Jordan (applied-ml): Quick update from the per-layer outlier sweep on Llama-3-8B across AWQ, GPTQ-INT8 and FP8 profiles. Ran per-layer stats + quant-error sim, then evaluated on the 10k validation prompts. Sending a short summary below.
Mia (ml-eng): awesome — numbers?
Jordan (applied-ml): TL;DR: AWQ-int8 with per-channel outlier scaling gives the best quality/latency balance. Numbers (median over prompts): AWQ-int8: avg EM drop ~0.9%, mean token perplexity +1.2%. GPTQ-int8: EM drop ~2.4%, PP +3.1%. FP8 (bfloat-ish): EM drop ~0.3%, PP +0.4%.
Jordan (applied-ml): Per-layer findings: layers with the highest reconstruction error and activation skew were L8, L12, L20. Those layers contain a small set of outlier channels (~3-5 per layer) with very large L-inf values that dominate quantization error.
Raj (infra): skipping layers helps quality but what about perf/cost?
Jordan (applied-ml): Short perf note: skipping those 3 layers (keeping them fp16) increases model footprint by ~1.2GB and end-to-end latency +6.5% on a single p4d instance. AWQ-int8 + per-channel rescale (no skipping) increases latency only +3.2% vs fully fp16 baseline but keeps most of the quality (EM drop ~0.9).
Sophia (sre): For hosted customers, is the latency delta acceptable? Any regressions that trigger fallbacks?
Jordan (applied-ml): For hosted: recommend AWQ-int8 + outlier scaling as default for PLG tiers. For enterprise SLAs that cannot tolerate >1% quality drop, recommend skip-layer for those 3 layers or enable mixed-precision fallback. We can automate model routing: prefer AWQ-int8 for standard, fallback to skip-layer profile when eval metrics on customer's prompt set exceed thresholds.
Mia (ml-eng): How are we detecting the outlier channels? code?
Jordan (applied-ml): detection pipeline was simple: gather activation distribution per-channel on a representational calibration set, compute z-score and L-inf ratio vs median channel. Flag channels where z>6 or max_ratio>20. Then compute expected quant reconstruction MSE and rank channels by delta.
Mia (ml-eng): can you paste the snippet?
Jordan (applied-ml): sure — paste below (pseudo):
```python
# compute per-channel max and std over calibration activations
for layer in layers:
    act = activations[layer]  # shape: [N, C] after flattening spatial/tokens
    max_per_channel = act.max(axis=0)
    std_per_channel = act.std(axis=0)
    z = (max_per_channel - np.median(max_per_channel)) / (np.std(max_per_channel) + 1e-8)
    outlier_mask = (z > 6) | (max_per_channel / (np.median(max_per_channel)+1e-6) > 20)
    outlier_channels = np.where(outlier_mask)[0]
    # propose scaling factor per outlier channel
    scale = np.minimum( max_per_channel / (np.percentile(max_per_channel,95)+1e-9), 8.0 )
    channel_scales[layer] = scale
```
Jordan (applied-ml): Then during quant we apply per-channel clipping/scaling before weight quantization and optionally run bias correction for those channels. This reduces per-channel quant error by ~60% on the flagged channels.
Raj (infra): What about GPTQ-specific mitigations?
Jordan (applied-ml): For GPTQ we tried group-wise reconstruction and per-channel rescale but it didn't close the gap as well as AWQ's outlier-aware kernels. GPTQ still benefits from skipping the top-3 outlier channels per layer for the worst layers.
Sophia (sre): Any impact on KV-cache memory or serving path complexity for mixed profiles?
Jordan (applied-ml): Minor. Mixed precision increases memory metadata by ~40MB for masks/scales and a tiny dispatch overhead. KV-cache unchanged. Complexity is in deploy-time profile selection.
Eli (devex): I can add a recommendation to Redwood Optimize — flag these layers and surface a profile toggle: AWQ-int8 (recommended), AWQ-int8+outlier-scaling (default for sensitive customers), AWQ-int8+skip-layers (strict-quality). Want a PR with the recommended thresholds.
Jordan (applied-ml): yes please. Next steps: 1) run full 50k prompt bakeoff across the three profiles (AWQ-int8 + scaling, AWQ-int8 + skip-layers, GPTQ-int8). 2) create perf/cost table per deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private). 3) open PR with quant configs and per-layer masks.
Mia (ml-eng): I'll kick off the 50k run tonight. leaving a note: use diverse prompt buckets (prod, long-context, code, math).
